terms.gloss: judge: weigh up and decide; hold, consider
evidence: Ter. Ad. 564: abī, virum tē jūdicō
Cic. Amic. 85: cum jūdicāris, dīligere oportet
terms.comment: To try a case and to judge in the everyday sense alike. With a double accusative, judge someone to be: virum tē jūdicō, I judge you a man. From which one can judge: ex quō … jūdicārī potest (Cic. Amic. 23).

terms.gloss: judge between, decide which is right
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: to judge by discerning or distinguishing; to decide, determine.

phrases.latin: Laudō, Ctēsiphō; patrissās: abī, virum tē jūdicō.
phrases.english: Well done, Ctesipho, you take after your father. Off you go: I judge you a man.

phrases.latin: cum jūdicāris, dīligere oportet, nōn, cum dīlēxeris, jūdicāre
phrases.english: you should judge first and then love, not love first and then judge

phrases.latin: Ex quō quantum bonī sit in amīcitiā jūdicārī potest.
phrases.english: From this one can judge how much good there is in friendship.

sources: Lewis & Short: judico · Lewis & Short: dijudico
